sites.whatWorks: A stacked three-line wordmark doubling as the hero headline, near-white/slate palette with a single powder-blue accent used almost nowhere, and zero biomarker UI on the homepage — trust is carried entirely by full-bleed photography and vocabulary, proving a longevity brand can read as pure hospitality.
sites.avoid: Depends entirely on exceptional consistent photography; has no data/dashboard content on the homepage at all, so it's a poor fit if biomarker visualization needs to be the hero.

sites.whatWorks: A serif display face (Orleans) on a body-scanning AI-health brand plus a pastel sky-blue base (not saturated clinical blue) with a single yellow closing-CTA band breaks the SaaS-dashboard default entirely.
sites.avoid: Withholds almost all quantitative/biomarker content from the homepage; low-contrast muted text colors on pale backgrounds need legibility checks at small sizes.

sites.whatWorks: A light editorial serif with italic keyword emphasis over warm cream/terracotta carries rigorously data-forward content (a row-by-row highlighted comparison table, a credentialed doctor grid) — proves 'scientific' and 'warm/editorial' aren't mutually exclusive.
sites.avoid: Shares its exact type/colour system with Ezra in this dataset (same design agency) — this specific serif+terracotta combination is becoming a recognizable DTC-health-tech cliche; vary it for differentiation.

sites.whatWorks: A rotating ghost-type word list in the hero (Fitness/Nutrition/DNA/Blood/Sleep) visualizes data breadth without a chart, and a phone-mockup dashboard with a circular score + red/green traffic-light recommendations is the clearest 'biological score' pattern in the dataset.
sites.avoid: Bold-grotesk hero plus green accent is close to generic wellness-app default; the pattern only stands out because of the animated word-list device — don't use the palette alone.

sites.whatWorks: A full-bleed magenta/burgundy gradient section built entirely around one radial dot-ring 'epigenetic age: 43' visualization turns a single biomarker into the site's most dramatic, memorable moment, breaking the clinical-blue category default entirely.
sites.avoid: Light-weight custom sans on saturated magenta backgrounds needs careful contrast checking; back-to-back saturated sections without cream breathing room between them would fatigue fast.

sites.whatWorks: Awwwards SOTD; achieves a 'dark/high-tech' mood on a pure white-background site purely through warm backlit photography and a floating tablet dashboard mockup mid-page, with one orange accent restricted to icon strokes only.
sites.avoid: Very long whitespace gaps between sections in the full-page view risk feeling sparse; the icon-only accent use is subtle and can get lost without reinforcement elsewhere.

sites.whatWorks: Near-black base with one glowing cyan-to-blue family applied consistently across every feature card, plus a named, visually-branded AI concierge ('Zori AI Medical Expert') that makes an abstract 'AI-powered' claim concrete.
sites.avoid: Uniform glow-panel treatment across every card can feel sample-like if not varied by composition; needs generous black negative space between glowing elements to avoid eye strain.

sites.whatWorks: Itemized, transparent scan pricing (exact currency, exact minutes, exact included body regions) removes ambiguity most diagnostic-scan competitors leave vague; pairs one dramatic mortality statistic with a real patient testimonial instead of a chart.
sites.avoid: Identical type/colour system to Function Health in this dataset — already a recognizable DTC-health-tech serif cliche; vary the accent hue or serif if differentiation matters.

sites.whatWorks: A black-to-teal radial gradient hero with warm candid (not stock) photography of real couples/athletes blends the dark-tech and warm-human poles; a 7-person named clinician headshot grid plus institutional/press logos gives the most credential-dense trust section in the set.
sites.avoid: Dark hero photography needs a strong scrim to keep white headline text legible; a 7-person credential grid needs uniform small headshots or it will overwhelm the page.

sites.whatWorks: Structured as a supplement/ecommerce product catalogue rather than a clinic-booking site, with a cool navy-on-cream base and an unexpected saturated violet-blue accent (not the category's usual green/teal/terracotta) — proves longevity branding doesn't require spa or clinical cues at all.
sites.avoid: Trust model depends on a famous founder's personal brand and self-experimentation; harder to port without an equivalently public figure, and the broader brand carries grift criticism worth noting but not borrowing.

clusters.label: Clinical-Luxury / Quiet Premium
clusters.summary: Restrained, editorial, near-achromatic bases where full-bleed photography and a single humanist or serif display face carry the entire brand. Lanserhof pushes furthest into pure hospitality — a stacked wordmark hero, zero biomarker UI, and a powder-blue accent used almost nowhere. Neko Health sits at the scientific border of this cluster: a genuine serif headline (Orleans) over a pastel sky-blue/yellow palette signals calm, considered hardware rather than a dashboard-first health-tech product. Both prove that 'longevity clinic' doesn't require clinical blue or visible data to read as credible.

clusters.label: Scientific / Data-Forward
clusters.summary: Each site turns a single measurement into its own signature visual moment rather than defaulting to a generic chart: Function Health's row-by-row highlighted comparison table (Function vs. average checkup), InsideTracker's phone-mockup circular score with red/green traffic-light recommendations, and Tally Health's full-bleed magenta radial dot-ring 'epigenetic age: 43' reveal. Ranges from warm-editorial-serif (Function) to green-coaching-app (InsideTracker) to loud fashion-magenta (Tally) — proving data-forward doesn't mean visually uniform.

clusters.label: Dark / High-Tech / Near-Futurist
clusters.summary: Superpower achieves this mood on a white-background site through warm backlit photography, a floating tablet-dashboard mockup, and one orange accent restricted to icon strokes — proving 'high-tech' doesn't require a literal dark UI. Fountain Life goes fully near-black with a glowing cyan-to-blue family applied uniformly across every feature card and a named, visually-branded AI concierge ('Zori'). Together they show two different routes to a futurist, AI-forward mood: one through photography and restraint, one through literal dark-mode glow.

clusters.label: Warm / Human / Trust-First
clusters.summary: Ezra and Prenuvo both lean on real, credentialed clinicians and candid (not stock) photography over warm cream or a black-to-teal gradient — Ezra adds unusually transparent itemized pricing, Prenuvo adds a 7-person named clinical team and press-heavy social proof. Blueprint breaks furthest from the pack: an ecommerce-first supplement catalogue in cool navy-on-cream with an unexpected violet-blue accent, trading clinician trust for founder-driven, self-experimentation credibility — proof this category can be sold as a purchasable protocol rather than an in-person clinic experience.
